transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~55 mins
Attendees: Sophie Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Anya Li (Redwood CSM), Priya Kaur (Head of ML - Marlin), Ethan Price (Infra Lead), Leah Marsh (CPO), Samir Patel (Finance)

Summary:
Quick QBR/check-in after last week's incident where Marlin saw a token-level usage spike. Main goals: understand root cause (prompt mix + bursty traffic), map cost impact, agree on a stress-test plan and short pilot guardrails, and confirm security/network constraints for a dedicated pilot environment.

Topics:
- Incident recap and traffic characterization
- Token-economics and per-route cost breakdown
- Reliability: autoscale, warm-up, KV cache behavior (sometimes mis-transcribed as KV cash)
- Pilot stress-test plan and timelines
- Compliance doc requests (SOC2 / pen test / KMS)

Action items recap (spoken during meeting):
- Priya to share traffic traces and sample prompt distributions
- Marco and Ethan to set up a staging stress window and check network egress limits
- Sophie to send detailed cost breakdown and pilot proposal
- Anya to share security package

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to make this a tight 45-ish minute sync but, um, leave room for the stress test planning. Quick check — is this still the right group?
[00:07] Priya: Yep, this is Priya — thanks. I'll add, we've got Samir sitting in for finance questions.
[00:12] Samir: hi all, yeah, I'm here.
[00:15] Marco: Cool. Quick agenda — one: what happened during the spike, two: cost impact, three: reliability mitigations, four: plan for a controlled stress test.
[00:25] Ethan: I can start with infra notes we saw — we had a short window where concurrency doubled for about 18 minutes, total tokens per minute spiked, and our autoscaler hit a few thresholds which caused a brief queueing. Nothing catastrophic but latency went up to ~1.2s p90 from 300ms baseline.
[00:42] Priya: Yeah so that was when our new prompt variant (customer-summary plus enrichment) rolled out — turns out the enrichment path adds around 40% more tokens, and because of an early batch job it coincided with a marketing drip so traffic overlapped.
[00:58] Leah: Is that the aggregation job? We thought it was behind a different queue.
[01:03] Priya: Right, sorry, the aggregation was the older one; the new enrichment ran inline in some user flows so the combination was the issue.
[01:12] Sophie: Okay so two contributors: prompt token increase and an overlapping job. Marco, what did you see on the Redwood side in terms of per-request behavior?
[01:20] Marco: We saw wider tails on sequence lengths, and because you had a lot more long contexts the KV cache warmed more slowly — sometimes the KV "cash" behavior was a bit off in the transcriptions I saw from the logs, but it's KV cache. Also the model selection did a fallback to a higher-cost variant for a subset due to latency SLOs, that bumped unit cost.
[01:40] Samir: Can you quantify "bumped unit cost"? Our budget team is, like, really nervous.
[01:45] Sophie: Sure, we ran a short costing snapshot — rough numbers: baseline token cost for your routes was ~$0.005/token equivalent, during the spike the effective cost rose about 38% because of the longer sequences and a handful of fallbacks to the higher-quality instance. We'll send the full per-route breakdown.
[02:05] Samir: Okay we need that in writing.
[02:08] Sophie: Yep, action item.
[02:12] Priya: One nuance — some prompts are amplified by the internal paraphrase layer, which frankly doubles tokens for certain flows. We should include that in the sample prompts.
[02:23] Marco: Good note. For reliability mitigations we have three levers: smarter batching thresholds, prefix/KV caching tuning, and a routing rule to prefer cheaper model variants when cost exceed thresholds — with a canary for quality checks.
[02:37] Ethan: On our side, we can gate the marketing drip or throttle it, but we'd prefer Redwood to help us test the system under anticipated load so we can see the end-to-end behavior.
[02:47] Marco: Absolutely, we recommend a staged stress test — start with a 30-minute ramp to target concurrency, then a sustained 6-hour window, then a cool-down. That gives you data on autoscaler churn, KV cache hit-rate, and fallback behavior.
[03:01] Leah: 6 hours sounds long, any cost estimate?
[03:05] Sophie: We'll estimate, but the value is you catch long-tail effects and the cost is predictable. We'll include an estimate in the breakdown.
[03:11] Priya: For the stress test we need to replicate the prompt mix and the paraphrase amplification. Priya: I'll export the prompt samples and distributions after this call.
[03:19] Sophie: Great, so next — network and security. Ethan, you had a question about private peering and egress?
[03:25] Ethan: Yeah, on our side we need to confirm egress caps; also if we do a private deployment we need KMS integration for envelope encryption.
[03:33] Anya: We can provide the KMS integration guide and our SOC2 attestation. We'll send pen-test summaries too.
[03:38] Ethan: Good. Also, does Redwood keep per-token-level logs or do we only see aggregated traces? We need auditability for compliance.
[03:46] Marco: We provide detailed tracing hooks and request-level metadata. For full logging we can configure retention and redaction rules; we never store raw PII unless you opt in, and logs can be integrated with your Splunk/Datadog.
[03:57] Priya: Is that under the Private offering or Hosted?
[04:00] Marco: Both, but Private gives you more control over retention and KMS. Hosted can be configured to meet many enterprise needs but if strict network egress and customer-managed KMS are required, Private is the path.
[04:12] Leah: Cost delta — any rough ranges between Hosted and Private for a reserved pilot?
[04:17] Sophie: Typically Private has an upfront platform fee plus infra costs and support — for a 3-month pilot we can model a blended rate; we'll put numbers in the proposal.
[04:25] Samir: From finance perspective we'll evaluate the blended model vs. staying on Hosted and adding throttles.
[04:31] Marco: One more reliability note: if you expect bursty marketing windows, setting a short warm pool of reserved capacity or a predictable dedicated lane reduces fallback and unit-cost volatility.
[04:42] Priya: That could help. But we need to validate in staging first.
[04:46] Sophie: So plan of record: we run a staged stress test in a Redwood staging environment that mirrors your on-prem proxies and prompt mix. Marco will own the test orchestration and Ethan will configure VPC/networking.
[04:58] Leah: Timeline?
[05:00] Marco: Proposed date is 2026-07-16 for the sustained 6-hour window, with a ramp test earlier in the week to smoke-test the harness.
[05:07] Priya: That works for the ML team.
[05:09] Ethan: I'll try to clear the 16th on infra side.
[05:12] Samir: Finance will need a cost cap for the experiment. Can we set a hard budget?
[05:16] Sophie: Yep we can set a cap and include alerts. We'll also include per-route cost warnings so you don't get surprised.
[05:22] Priya: Another small item — prompt engineering team wants to test quantization options; is that part of the stress test or separate?
[05:28] Marco: We can include one quantized model variant as part of a later A/B in the test, but initial run should focus on raw traffic characteristics.
[05:35] Priya: Okay makes sense.
[05:36] [10:00] (sketchy longer section — people cross-talking about exact test harness and sample sizes; some timestamps and words got clipped)
[10:30] Priya: We'll provide the exact sample sizes and p95/p99 goals.
[10:35] Marco: On logs and metrics we'll provide a dashboard template — CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, model fallbacks, and token consumption per route.
[10:45] Sophie: Any blockers to scheduling the stress test?
[10:48] Ethan: Our main blocker is gating the production drip; we need to ensure the marketing team can pause if required. We'll coordinate.
[10:56] Leah: Also want to confirm SLA expectations during the pilot — are we covered?
[11:00] Sophie: For pilots we provide operational support; SLA for Dedicated is different from hosted, we'll clarify in proposal.
[11:06] Samir: Please include escalation contacts.
[11:09] Anya: I'll include a support matrix and SRE on-call handoff details.
[11:14] Priya: One more tiny point — the paraphrase amplification was not uniform; some user segments had higher impact. We'll mark those in the traces.
[11:22] Marco: Good. That'll help us tune caching and batching profiles.
[11:27] Sophie: OK we've got the follow-ups. Can we run through explicit next steps so we capture ownership?
[11:33] Ethan: I'll open the VPC peering ticket and confirm egress limits by Monday.
[11:38] Priya: I'll export prompts and traffic traces today and upload to the shared sftp link.
[11:43] Samir: Finance will review the proposed cost cap and get back with red lines.
[11:48] Sophie: I'll send the cost breakdown and pilot proposal with suggested success metrics by Monday as well. Marco will share the staging runbook. Anya will send SOC2 + pen test summary.
[11:59] Leah: Sounds good.
[12:02] Sophie: Alright thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the thread and confirm the 7/16 window.
[12:07] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: Several segments had crosstalk and a short audio drop around 10:00-10:40 where some lines were clipped. Proper nouns like "KV cache" were sometimes transcribed as "KV cash" and model variant names were omitted in the live notes.

Recap (spoken):
- Immediate: Sophie sends cost breakdown; Anya sends security package; Priya/Ethan provide traces and network constraints.
- Mid: Marco schedules staging stress test (ramp + 6-hour sustained) targeted 2026-07-16.
- Long: Follow-up QBR week of 2026-07-20 to review results and pilot next steps.
